vendored.name: qnxprobe
vendored.note: Reads the file systems the rest of this program cannot: QNX6, QNX4, ETFS, EFS, QNX IFS, F2FS, SquashFS, JFFS2, UBI/UBIFS, YAFFS1/2, Btrfs, XFS, ReFS and more. Copied verbatim; fix upstream and re-vendor rather than editing here.

vendored.name: ewfprobe
vendored.note: Reads an EnCase/EWF .E01 acquisition without libewf. Copied verbatim; fix upstream and re-vendor rather than editing here.

vendored.name: qnxmount (specifications only)
vendored.note: No code from qnxmount is here. qnxprobe transcribes its Kaitai byte-layout specifications for QNX ETFS and EFS, and its licence travels with that work.

vendored.name: c2pareader
vendored.why: Reads the Content Credentials a file declares, from seven container formats, and says whether its walk was complete -- which is what makes an absent manifest mean anything. Verifies nothing, which is stated wherever it is used.

vendored.name: exoprobe
vendored.why: Rebuilds video an Android app streamed. ExoPlayer stores one video as numbered pieces with its name in a separate index, so the pieces are unplayable and nameless until they are joined. Also joins DASH and HLS segments in the order the cached manifest lists them.

vendored.name: mediacarve
vendored.note: Copied verbatim from GLEAPP's vendored copy, which records the same SHA-256 for upstream commit 81dbe9e7189a50f94f1e3e002096b3e66aee7845. Fix upstream and re-vendor rather than editing here.
vendored.why: The carve's judge of where a file starts and ends (fme/engines/carve_judge.py). It walks each format's own structure before claiming bytes, never lets a length it could not confirm hide a later file, and says how each length was arrived at: header, parsed or capped. That label is the manifest's bounded column.
